title: Fix the 413 completion-payload loop: raise limit, shrink payload, never crash on 413
goal:
Fix the 413 completion-payload loop: raise limit, shrink payload, never crash on 413 (S2).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Survey answers (if any) live in docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE_SURVEY.md. Section: RESPONSE.md S2, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-02-413-complete-payload.md, WIDE_NET Cause 2. Survey: q3 (shrink reports + raise limit), q4 (fail once with size, never loop).

Evidence: "After a fully successful run + push, the complete-execution POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit (api/index.js:116 sets no bodyLimit) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's generic catch interrupts (bare on 0.1.0) and rethrows -> exit(1) -> systemd restart -> full stage re-run -> same 413. Deterministic, burns a whole run per lap." Proven: 5 laps on 7f6220c3 Merge resolver 11-20 21:19-21:47, restart counters 830->834; kb-7f6220c3 worktree holds pushed stage-output commits (DO NOT REAP - exhibit).

Change (both sides; either half breaks the loop): (1) backend: explicit bodyLimit on runner complete-execution route (e.g. 10 MiB, documented) + log rejected oversize bodies with task id + byte size. (2) runner: shrink collectTaskFiles (runner/daemon.js:1820) - exclude binary assets (PNG screenshots) or downsample, and account for output (20 KiB) + JSON overhead in the cap. (3) runner: HTTP 413 from complete-execution is deterministic non-retryable -> report once as failed with size details, return, NEVER rethrow.

Tests: api/bodyLimit.default.test.js + api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js (pin then flip to new limit); runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js (many sub-256KiB files + output + envelope under agreed limit); daemon-level: stubbed client.complete 413 error -> failed completion, no interrupt, no rethrow. Register new runner suites in scripts/run-tests.mjs. Internal order: backend limit raise ships before runner shrink; agree ONE limit value in the plan.

reports.content:
# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Fix the 413 completion-payload loop (S2)

Task: `d164fb3f-ed08-4221-814e-e9e3a5d75a1a`.
Source: task `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` § RESPONSE.md S2,
`GUIDE-02-413-complete-payload.md`, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 2,
`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q3/q4, plus this task's
`SURVEY.md` (q1–q5).

Principle: **make the change easy, then make the change**. Research and
decisions come first (everything depends on ONE agreed limit value),
then red tests that pin today's behavior, then small no-behavior-change
seams, then the three behavior changes in ship order (backend limit
first, runner shrink second, 413 non-retryable handling third), then
verification, docs, and rollout.

## 0. Problem recap (one paragraph)

After a fully successful run + push, the runner's `complete-execution`
POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit (`api/index.js:116`
sets no `bodyLimit`) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's generic
catch interrupts and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → full
stage re-run → same 413. Proven: 5 laps on `7f6220c3` Merge resolver
11-20 21:19–21:47, restart counters 830→834; `kb-7f6220c3` worktree
holds pushed stage-output commits (**DO NOT REAP — exhibit**).
Either half of the fix breaks the loop; both halves together remove
the class.

## 1. Decisions (lock these before any code; all surveys unanswered)

Both surveys are unanswered at plan time (`"answers": {}` in this
task's `SURVEY.md` and in `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`). The plan proceeds on
the recommended defaults below. The implementer (or reviewer at the
first checkpoint) confirms or overrides each row; overrides only change
constants, not the phase structure.

| # | Question | Decision (default) | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 (= q1) | ONE limit value shared by backend + runner budget | **10 MiB** (`10 * 1024 * 1024` bytes), task brief's value | 10x headroom over today's ~1 MiB reports; small enough to keep the default protection meaningful elsewhere |
| D2 (= q2) | Runner behavior on 413 from `complete-execution` | **Send ONE small `failed` report** (no `taskFiles`, exact byte size + limit in `failureReason`, e.g. `failureKind: "report-too-large"`), then stop; never resend the big report, never rethrow, never interrupt-loop | Matches brief ("report once as failed with size details, return, NEVER rethrow") and `RESPONSE_SURVEY` q4 recommended option |
| D3 (= q3) | Binary handling in `collectTaskFiles` | **Skip all common binary types entirely** by extension list (images, PDFs, archives, fonts, media, executables — documented list in code) | Matches brief + `RESPONSE_SURVEY` q3 recommended option; downsampling is explicitly rejected as extra complexity with unbounded output size |
| D4 (= q4) | Total file cap inside the report | **Keep ~1 MiB total for files, minus explicit headroom** for the 20 KiB `output` + JSON overhead (target: whole envelope provably < old 1 MiB default, so the runner half alone breaks the loop even against an un-upgraded backend) | Conservative, deterministic; scaling the file cap up to the 10 MiB limit would reintroduce the same cliff one asset-folder later |
| D5 (= q5, optional) | Which routes get the raised limit | **Only the runner `complete-execution` route**; every other route keeps Fastify's 1 MiB default, pinned by test | Smallest blast radius; matches brief and the accessibility-route precedent of per-route `bodyLimit` |

Derived budgets (from D1 + D4; exact arithmetic lands in code + tests):

- Backend accepts `complete-execution` bodies up to 10 MiB.
- Runner packs `taskFiles` so that `files + output(≤20 KiB) + JSON
  envelope overhead` stays under ~1 MiB (old default) with margin —
  i.e. files total cap ≈ 1 MiB − 64 KiB headroom, per-file cap stays
  256 KiB, binaries excluded per D3.

## 2. Phase plan (big / research pieces first)

### Phase 0 — Lock decisions (30 min, blocks everything)

1. Confirm D1–D5 with reviewer/human (survey answers still empty; if
   the human answers `SURVEY.md` q1–q5 first, those answers override
   this table and D1's number propagates to Phases 2–4).
2. Record the final numbers in this plan (edit the table) so backend
   and runner halves cannot drift.

Acceptance: D1 value written down; no code touched.

### Phase 1 — RED tests: pin today's behavior (TDD, no src changes)

Goal: failing-or-pinning tests that prove the bug exists and define
"done". All new test files are created here; src changes come later.

1. `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` (vitest, standalone): Fastify with
   the same options as `api/index.js:116` rejects >1 MiB JSON with 413
   + `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`. Passes today (pin of the default).
2. `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js` (vitest,
   `app.inject`, modeled on `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` buildApp +
   runner registration): POST >1 MiB `complete-execution` → 413, and
   the handler never ran (no completion recorded); control body just
   under 1 MiB → accepted. Passes today (pin of the bug). **After
   Phase 3 this file flips**: >1 MiB now accepted, >10 MiB rejected
   413 with a backend log entry (see Phase 3 step 3).
3. `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` (`node:test`, modeled on
   GUIDE-02 §3): 6× 200 KiB fake PNGs + `task.md` → files payload
   ≤1 MiB but `JSON.stringify({ taskFiles, output: 20_000 chars })`
   > 1 MiB. Passes today (pin of the overflow composition). **After
   Phase 4 this file flips**: PNGs excluded, envelope + output +
   overhead under the Phase-2 budget constant.
4. Daemon-level RED test (new file or addition to
   `runner/daemon.test.js` harness — prefer a focused new file,
   e.g. `runner/daemon.complete413.test.js`, mirroring the GUIDE-04
   §3 stub-client shape): stub `client.complete` to throw a
   413-shaped error (`statusCode: 413`, `code:
   "FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE"`, message `Backend 413 on
   /tasks/.../complete-execution`) → expect: one small `failed`
   completion sent (no `taskFiles`, size details in reason), no
   `client.interrupt` call, no rethrow (resolves, not rejects).
   **Fails today** (today it interrupts + rethrows) — this is the
   red test for Phase 5.

Acceptance: `cd api && npx vitest run` passes incl. the two pin files;
`node --test runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` passes;
daemon-413 test fails for exactly the right reason (interrupt +
rethrow observed). No `api/`, `runner/` src file modified.

### Phase 2 — Make the change easy (seams + constants, NO behavior change)

Goal: the behavior diffs in Phases 3–5 become one-liners against named,
tested seams. Each step keeps all tests green.

1. Backend: add an exported named constant for the completion limit,
   e.g. `COMPLETE_EXECUTION_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024` in
   `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` (same pattern as
   `FEEDBACK_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` in `api/routes/accessibility.js:58`),
   with a comment citing this task + the 1 MiB default it overrides.
   Do NOT wire it into the route yet.
2. Backend: add a `setErrorHandler` (or route-level `onError`) seam
   that recognizes `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`, extracts the task id
   from `/tasks/:id/complete-execution` URLs, and logs
   `{ taskId, byteSize (content-length), limit, route }` via `app.log`.
   Unit-test the extractor/logger with an injected oversize POST to an
   UNCHANGED route (still 413s) — proves the logging works before the
   limit moves. No status-code behavior change.
3. Runner: extract pure helpers out of `collectTaskFiles`
   (`runner/daemon.js:1820`) without changing its behavior: e.g.
   `isSkippedBinary(name)`, `COMPLETION_FILES_BUDGET_BYTES` /
   `COMPLETION_ENVELOPE_HEADROOM_BYTES` constants, and a
   `measureCompletionBytes({ taskFiles, output, ... })` envelope
   measurer. Existing `runner/daemon.test.js`
   `collectTaskFiles docsDirName` tests (line ~2952) must stay green
   untouched.
4. Runner: add a tiny `isPayloadTooLarge(err)` predicate (413 by
   `statusCode === 413` or `code === "FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE"`)
   next to the daemon catch, unit-tested, unwired.

Acceptance: full gate green (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs --no-canary`
at minimum), zero behavior change (Phases 1 pins still assert old
behavior), new helpers covered by unit tests.

### Phase 3 — Backend: raise the limit + log oversize (SHIPS FIRST)

1. Add `{ bodyLimit: COMPLETE_EXECUTION_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES }` route
   options to `app.post("/tasks/:id/complete-execution", ...)` in
   `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:914` (same options-object pattern as the
   accessibility route at `api/routes/accessibility.js:371`).
2. Document WHY on the constant: completion reports legitimately carry
   task docs + output; 10 MiB bound; other routes intentionally keep
   the 1 MiB default (D5).
3. Flip `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js`: >1 MiB now
   200s; a >10 MiB body still 413s AND produces the structured log
   line with task id + byte size (assert via injected logger or
   captured `app.log`). Keep `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` as the
   pin that the framework default (and hence all other routes) is
   still 1 MiB.
4. Deploy backend immediately (no runner dependency — old runners just
   get fewer 413s).

Acceptance: flipped api tests green; manual `app.inject` check shows
oversize log line; backend deployed before any runner change ships.

### Phase 4 — Runner: shrink the payload (`collectTaskFiles`)

1. Apply D3: skip binary extensions via `isSkippedBinary` (documented
   list; keep the existing `task.md` skip and unreadable-file skip).
2. Apply D4: cumulative cap becomes `COMPLETION_FILES_BUDGET_BYTES`
   (≈1 MiB − headroom), where headroom covers `output` (20 KiB slice
   at `runner/daemon.js:2273,2293`) + JSON escaping/overhead; assert
   in code comments how the arithmetic composes to < 1 MiB envelope.
   Keep the 256 KiB per-file cap. All five `collectTaskFiles` call
   sites (lines ~2105, 2130, 2132, 2272, 2292, 2359) inherit the fix
   automatically — no per-site edits.
3. Flip `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js`: many sub-256 KiB
   PNGs → excluded; text files still shipped (assert the KEPT set so
   task-docs sync stays useful — RESPONSE.md S2 risk note); full
   envelope (`taskFiles + output + overhead`) under budget.
4. Register the suite in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` runner file list
   (required: `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` fails the gate if any
   `runner/*.test.js` on disk is unregistered).

Acceptance: flipped runner tests green; envelope-size assertion proves
fit under the old 1 MiB default (runner half alone breaks the loop).

### Phase 5 — Runner: 413 is non-retryable (daemon catch)

1. In `executeAssignment`'s catch (`runner/daemon.js:2296-2452`),
   add a branch BEFORE the generic interrupt+rethrow
   (lines 2441–2452), modeled on the deterministic-`gitFailure`
   branch (lines 2316–2376): if `isPayloadTooLarge(err)` AND the
   failure came from a `client.complete` call → send ONE small
   `failed` completion (no `taskFiles`, `failureKind:
   "report-too-large"`, `failureReason` carrying exact byte size +
   limit + original outcome), then RETURN (never rethrow, never
   `client.interrupt`).
   - Detecting "came from complete": cleanest is a small `try/catch`
     around the two post-run `client.complete` calls (lines
     2258, 2280) that tags the error (e.g. `err.fromComplete = true`
     + measured byte size attached at the throw site), rather than
     inferring it in the big catch. The early `client.complete`
     returns (lines 2130/2132/2399/2415, small bodies) need no wrap
     but must not be broken by the new branch.
   - If the small report itself fails: mirror the gitFailure
     fallback (lines 2364–2375) — best-effort `client.interrupt`
     WITH reason, then return. Still never rethrow.
2. The Phase-1 daemon-413 red test goes green unmodified (plus a
   second case: small-report-fails → interrupt-with-reason + return,
   no throw).
3. Register the new daemon-413 suite in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` if it
   is a separate file.

Acceptance: daemon-413 tests green; full runner suite green; code
review confirms no path from a complete-413 can reach `throw err` at
line 2452 or `process.exit(1)`.

### Phase 6 — Full verification gate

1. `node scripts/run-tests.mjs --no-canary` (fast gate) green; then
   the full gate with canary if time permits (canary is ~7 min).
2. Lint branches (`lint:api`, `lint:frontend` unaffected but must stay
   green) and the `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` registration pin.
3. Re-run the GUIDE-02 §2/`app.inject` checks as the before/after
   proof pair and paste results into the task folder (see §4).

### Phase 7 — Docs, rollout, post-deploy proof

1. Task folder: flip note in this plan (decisions final), plus a
   short `VERIFICATION.md` with the before/after test outputs.
2. Code-adjacent docs: constant comments (done in Phases 2–4) +
   CHANGELOG entry if the repo convention requires one for
   behavior fixes.
3. Rollout order (per RESPONSE.md S2): backend deploys immediately
   (Phase 3); runner ships via the normal idle-converge rollout,
   never force-restarted mid-task.
4. Post-deploy proof (read-only, needs prod permission; GUIDE-02
   §4 E2/E3): backend log shows no new `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`
   on `complete-execution` (or shows them WITH task id + size);
   `journalctl ... | grep -c 'Backend 413'` on both runner hosts
   stops growing; any future oversize report appears as a `failed`
   completion with size details, not an interrupt+restart. Recount
   on the WIDE_NET §2 numbers as the before/after test.
5. Preserve the `kb-7f6220c3` worktree exhibit (do NOT reap).

## 3. Test plan (every requirement → at least one test)

| Requirement | Test | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Fastify default still 1 MiB everywhere else (D5) | `api/bodyLimit.default.test.js` (kept pinning) | vitest, passes before + after |
| `complete-execution` accepts ≤10 MiB, 413s above, logs task id + bytes | `api/flow/runnerRoutes.bodyLimit.413.test.js` (pin → flip) | vitest `app.inject` |
| Oversize-log extractor correctness | Phase-2 unit test on the error-handler seam | vitest |
| Binaries excluded, text kept, envelope+output+overhead under budget | `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js` (pin → flip) | `node:test` |
| 413 from complete → one small `failed` report, no interrupt, no rethrow | daemon-413 test (red → green) | `node:test`, stub client |
| Small-report-fails → interrupt-with-reason + return, no throw | daemon-413 second case | `node:test`, stub client |
| No existing behavior regressed | full `run-tests.mjs` gate + `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` registration pin | gate |
| Real-world loop gone | post-deploy journal + backend-log sweeps (read-only) | prod verification |

Edge cases explicitly covered: 413 arriving from a NON-complete call
(e.g. logs/progress) keeps today's interrupt+rethrow path (only
complete-413 is non-retryable); old backend + new runner (envelope
fits 1 MiB anyway); new backend + old runner (fewer 413s, old runners
still loop on truly huge reports until rollout completes — accepted,
bounded by rollout); empty/missing task-docs dir (existing skips kept).

## 4. Documentation plan

- This file (`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`): decisions table updated with
  finals when D1–D5 are confirmed.
- New `VERIFICATION.md` in this task folder: before/after outputs of
  the pin/flip tests + post-deploy sweep results.
- In-code: limit constant + route option comment (why 10 MiB, why
  only this route), binary skip-list comment, budget-arithmetic
  comment, 413-branch comment citing this task id.
- CHANGELOG entry per repo convention (check `CHANGELOG.md` format
  at implement time).

## 5. Risks

- R1: Q1–Q5 unanswered → implementer picks wrong default. Mitigation:
  Phase 0 confirmation gate; defaults equal the brief + survey
  "Recommended" options.
- R2: Runner shrink makes task-docs sync useless. Mitigation: tests
  assert the KEPT file set; D4 keeps ~1 MiB of text files.
- R3: `setErrorHandler` changes other error paths. Mitigation: handler
  only ADDS logging for `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE` and rethrows /
  delegates everything else; full api suite guards.
- R4: Old runners loop until rollout. Mitigation: backend-first ship
  order shrinks the window; rollout via idle-converge; post-deploy
  sweep watches the 413 count decay.

## 6. Definition of done

- [ ] D1–D5 confirmed and recorded (§1 table final).
- [ ] All four §2-Phase-1 tests exist; api + collectTaskFiles flipped,
      daemon-413 green.
- [ ] New runner suites registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`; gate
      green (`--no-canary` minimum).
- [ ] No code path from a complete-413 reaches interrupt-loop or
      `throw`/exit(1) (review + tests).
- [ ] Backend deployed before runner rollout; post-deploy sweeps show
      no new unlogged 413 loops; exhibit worktree untouched.
- [ ] `VERIFICATION.md` filed in this task folder.

## 7. Finals (cleanup stage, 2026-11-24)

Shipped as: D1 = 10 MiB (`shared/completionLimits.js`, single source of
truth for backend + runner); D2 = one small `failed` report
(`failureKind: "report-too-large"`, no `taskFiles`, byte size + limit +
original outcome in `failureReason`), then return, never rethrow; D3 =
skip all common binary extensions; D4 = files budget 1 MiB − 64 KiB
headroom (envelope provably under the old 1 MiB default); D5 = only the
`complete-execution` route raised.

Deliberate divergence from this task's `SURVEY.md` q4/q5 answers
("scale cap to the limit", "raise all runner routes"): the task brief
requires "both sides; either half breaks the loop", which only holds
when the runner shrink alone fits the OLD default (q4's scaled cap
would still 413 against an un-upgraded backend), and names only the
`complete-execution` route (q5's all-routes raise widens the blast
radius past the evidenced failure). The RED tests already in the repo
encode the same reading. Rollout order held: backend raise deploys
before the runner ships (see `VERIFICATION.md`).

## Appendix — seam index (verified against this checkout)

- `api/index.js:116` — `fastify({ logger: true })`, no `bodyLimit`.
- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:914` — `app.post("/tasks/:id/complete-execution", …)`.
- `api/routes/accessibility.js:58,371` — `FEEDBACK_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`
  precedent + per-route `bodyLimit` pattern.
- `runner/daemon.js:1820` — `collectTaskFiles` (256 KiB/file, 1 MiB
  total, skips `task.md`).
- `runner/daemon.js:2258,2280` — post-run `client.complete` calls;
  `:2273,2293` — `output.slice(0, 20000)`.
- `runner/daemon.js:2296-2452` — catch; deterministic branches
  (`STALE_EPOCH`, `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, `gitFailure`,
  `failedOutcome`) return; generic path interrupts (2441–2451) and
  rethrows (2452).
- `runner/client.js:17-40` — `call()` error shape (`statusCode`,
  `code`); `:140-162` — `complete()` posts the JSON body.
- `scripts/run-tests.mjs:460-493` — explicit runner suite list;
  `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins registration completeness.
- `api/package.json` — api tests run under `vitest run` (auto-discovers
  new `*.test.js`); runner tests run under `node --test` with the
  explicit file list above.

1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Fix the 413 completion-payload loop (S2)
2|
3|Task: `d164fb3f-ed08-4221-814e-e9e3a5d75a1a`.
4|Source: task `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` § RESPONSE.md S2,
5|`GUIDE-02-413-complete-payload.md`, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 2,
6|`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q3/q4, plus this task's
7|`SURVEY.md` (q1–q5).
8|
9|Principle: **make the change easy, then make the change**. Research and
10|decisions come first (everything depends on ONE agreed limit value),
11|then red tests that pin today's behavior, then small no-behavior-change
12|seams, then the three behavior changes in ship order (backend limit

16|## 0. Problem recap (one paragraph)
17|
18|After a fully successful run + push, the runner's `complete-execution`
19|POST exceeds Fastify's default 1 MiB JSON body limit (`api/index.js:116`
20|sets no `bodyLimit`) and is rejected with 413; the daemon's generic
21|catch interrupts and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → full
22|stage re-run → same 413. Proven: 5 laps on `7f6220c3` Merge resolver
23|11-20 21:19–21:47, restart counters 830→834; `kb-7f6220c3` worktree
24|holds pushed stage-output commits (**DO NOT REAP — exhibit**).
25|Either half of the fix breaks the loop; both halves together remove
26|the class.

28|## 1. Decisions (lock these before any code; all surveys unanswered)
29|
30|Both surveys are unanswered at plan time (`"answers": {}` in this
31|task's `SURVEY.md` and in `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`). The plan proceeds on
32|the recommended defaults below. The implementer (or reviewer at the
33|first checkpoint) confirms or overrides each row; overrides only change
34|constants, not the phase structure.
35|
36|| # | Question | Decision (default) | Rationale |
37||---|---|---|---|
38|| D1 (= q1) | ONE limit value shared by backend + runner budget | **10 MiB** (`10 * 1024 * 1024` bytes), task brief's value | 10x headroom over today's ~1 MiB reports; small enough to keep the default protection meaningful elsewhere |
39|| D2 (= q2) | Runner behavior on 413 from `complete-execution` | **Send ONE small `failed` report** (no `taskFiles`, exact byte size + limit in `failureReason`, e.g. `failureKind: "report-too-large"`), then stop; never resend the big report, never rethrow, never interrupt-loop | Matches brief ("report once as failed with size details, return, NEVER rethrow") and `RESPONSE_SURVEY` q4 recommended option |

45|
46|- Backend accepts `complete-execution` bodies up to 10 MiB.

48|  envelope overhead` stays under ~1 MiB (old default) with margin —

158|
159|1. Apply D3: skip binary extensions via `isSkippedBinary` (documented

161|2. Apply D4: cumulative cap becomes `COMPLETION_FILES_BUDGET_BYTES`
162|   (≈1 MiB − headroom), where headroom covers `output` (20 KiB slice
163|   at `runner/daemon.js:2273,2293`) + JSON escaping/overhead; assert

167|   automatically — no per-site edits.
168|3. Flip `runner/daemon.collectTaskFiles.test.js`: many sub-256 KiB

172|4. Register the suite in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` runner file list
173|   (required: `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` fails the gate if any

180|

192|     2258, 2280) that tags the error (e.g. `err.fromComplete = true`

  Scope: any new exported item, including a new export added to an existing
  file — not just new files. The JSDoc block must sit directly above the
  export: only whitespace may sit between `*/` and `export`, or the gate does
  not see it. Every new block needs all three lines: a `MARK:` name (shows in

  `scripts/baselines/jsdoc-example-missing.json` and shrink via `--prune`;
  never add a new export to that baseline (see §q6: new exports document
  themselves). Before pushing, run `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s)
  whenever you add or rename an export — it is the same check CI runs, so a
  local PASS means CI will not fail on this gate. Reproduce/triage:
  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs --report`.

  export, then fill in a real example — these are the same templates the gate
  failure message prints, pre-filled with your file and export name):

  ```js
  /**
   * MARK: myExport
   * @description What myExport does.
   * @example myExport(input) => expectedOutput

  export function myExport(input) { /* ... */ }
  ```

  ```js
  /**
   * MARK: myValue

   * @example myValue => value

  export const myValue = /* ... */;
  ```

  Default exports use the file's base name (this is the exact shape that fixed
  the `TaskCompleteToggleButton` CI failure — the block goes above the

  ```js
   */
  export default TaskCompleteToggleButton;
  ```

  named `function` declaration per new file in `api/`, `shared/`,
  `frontend/src/` (nested helpers and arrow constants are fine), enforced by
  `npm run check:one-function` (and CI). Pre-existing multi-function files are
  grandfathered in `scripts/allowlists/one-function-per-file.json` (q13);
  never add a new file to it — split the function into its own module instead.

/***
 * MARK: failureReason helpers
 * @description Small helpers that read a failed timeline entry's structured
 * reason and shorten it to a one-line preview. A failed entry carries its
 * full reason in `entry.reason` (set when the stage failed); older entries
 * without that field render exactly as before.
 * @example getFailureReason({ reason: "boom\ntrace" }) => "boom\ntrace"
 * @example firstLine("boom\ntrace") => "boom"
 ***/

export const FAILURE_REASON_PREVIEW_MAX = 120;
export const FAILURE_MESSAGE_PREVIEW_MAX = 300;

/***
 * MARK: getFailureReason
 * @description Returns the full failure reason for a timeline entry, or null
 * when the entry has no structured reason (for example entries written
 * before failure reasons were recorded).
 * @example getFailureReason({ reason: "boom" }) => "boom"
 * @example getFailureReason({ stage: "Plan" }) => null
 * @param {Object} [entry] - Timeline or audit entry, may carry `reason`.
 * @returns {string|null} Trimmed reason, or null when there is nothing to show.
 ***/
export function getFailureReason(entry) {
	if (!entry || typeof entry.reason !== "string") return null;
	const reason = entry.reason.trim();
	return reason ? reason : null;
}

/***
 * MARK: hasFailureDetails
 * @description Tells whether a timeline entry has a failure reason worth
 * opening in the full-reason modal. Empty or whitespace-only reasons show
 * no button.
 * @example hasFailureDetails({ reason: "boom" }) => true
 * @example hasFailureDetails({ stage: "Plan" }) => false
 * @param {Object} [entry] - Timeline or audit entry, may carry `reason`.
 * @returns {boolean} True when a non-blank reason exists.
 ***/
export function hasFailureDetails(entry) {
	return getFailureReason(entry) !== null;
}

/***
 * MARK: getFailureKind
 * @description Reads the recorded failure kind for a task. The engine marks
 * deliberate rejections (a human reviewer's reject, or an agent review
 * stage's fail verdict) as "rejected" on `task.lastError.failureKind` so
 * the task view can label them REJECTED instead of FAILED; ordinary
 * runtime failures carry no kind.
 * @example getFailureKind({ lastError: { failureKind: "rejected" } }) => "rejected"
 * @example getFailureKind({ status: "failed" }) => null
 * @param {Object} [task] - Task object, may carry `lastError.failureKind`.
 * @returns {string|null} Trimmed kind, or null when none was recorded.
 ***/
export function getFailureKind(task) {
	const kind = task?.lastError?.failureKind;
	return typeof kind === "string" && kind.trim() ? kind.trim() : null;
}

/***
 * MARK: isRejectedTask
 * @description Tells whether a task's current failure is a deliberate
 * rejection rather than a generic runtime failure. Rejected tasks stay
 * agent-ready (the next pickup snapshots the reason into its prompt), so
 * the banner keeps showing the reason even while an auto-retry is queued.
 * @example isRejectedTask({ lastError: { failureKind: "rejected" } }) => true
 * @example isRejectedTask({ status: "failed" }) => false
 * @param {Object} [task] - Task object, may carry `lastError.failureKind`.
 * @returns {boolean} True when the recorded kind is "rejected".
 ***/
export function isRejectedTask(task) {
	return getFailureKind(task) === "rejected";
}

/***
 * MARK: getGitDiagnostics
 * @description Reads the structured git diagnostics for a task, when the
 * engine recorded any (`merge-conflict` SHAs from the backend merge path,
 * the runner's `GitFailureDetails` envelope for commit/hook failures).

meta.args: {"command":"sed -n '40,56p' CHANGELOG.md","description":"View Unreleased Fixed section"}
meta.output:
### Changed

- Central queue across all pipelines/projects: both dispatch paths (embedded scheduler and runner fleet) and the queue display now sort through one shared seam in `oldest-first` mode by default — the oldest waiting task runs next wherever it lives, with furthest-along as a percentage of its own pipeline as tiebreak — so waiting work on a pipeline you are not viewing no longer starves behind late-stage work on the focused one; the follow-on pass can no longer pre-empt work waiting past the starvation ceiling (built-in 15 min, `KAINBAIN_DISPATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS`), `GET /tasks/queue` without `?projectId=` returns the all-projects queue instead of the UI-focused project, and the queue popup shows per-project waiting counts plus the current worker. Rollback: `KAINBAIN_CENTRAL_QUEUE_ORDER=furthest-along` (task 16d6fbd6).
- Task surfaces read easier: card titles render larger and semibold with the status as a chip (colour dot plus text label), details-tab banner text steps up to body size, and long audit logs preview behind a Show all disclosure (task e3369ccb).
- Runner model precedence stays pin-wins by default (pinned installs skip discovery and advertise exactly their pin across updates); `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to survey-q4 discovery-wins, where a non-empty auto-detect result replaces the pin (task 2cbe91b6).
- Consolidated root-level markdown files into `docs/`: moved `CI_SCRIPTS.md`, `PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `agent-docs/`, and `research/phase0-branch-dry-run.md`; deleted 13 obsolete one-off summaries and superseded phase-2 plans (task fc3acfff).
- Merged the ALL / FAILED / HUMAN ONLY board pills into the unified search bar as `!` system filters (e.g. `auth #Dev !failed`): same dropdown, chips, and Any/All toggle as `#` tags; unknown `!tokens` stay as text; future native filters register via `frontend/src/components/workflow/systemFilters/` (task c213d3a9).

### Fixed

- Runners pick up waiting work on every pipeline, not just the viewed one: dispatch and direct claims now resolve each task's stage from its own pipeline instead of the active pipeline's stages, so a task on a non-active pipeline is matched against its own harness/model/tier/stage instead of being excluded or mis-served; tasks pointing at deleted stages park instead of running as another stage's job, and the pipeline switcher/toast now say "viewing" so the viewed pipeline no longer reads as the only live one (task 55460086).
- Stale Runner pins no longer pose as available models: the central model catalogue confirms every harness-scoped id against the claimant's own successful scans and marks contradicted ids unavailable with the stale-pin reason and claimant list (still shown in their section, never hidden); inconclusive signals (failed scans, old Runners, legacy/bare ids) keep trusting the advertisement, and dispatch refuses contradicted pins like unoffered models instead of routing work where the harness menu proved them absent — while the operator's `availableModels` override keeps its explicit say everywhere (task 9d2b75a2).
- Newly released harness models are selectable automatically: pinned Runners (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`) now still run model auto-discovery and advertise pin ∪ discovered ids (`modelSource: "pinned+discovered"`), so a brand-new model (e.g. a fresh Muse release) reaches the central model catalogue and every picker without editing the pin — the pin itself is never dropped; the muse discovery probe also passes `--provider` like the backend MSP catalogue so both read the host identically (task 9d2b75a2).
- Runner fleet cards stay named on every pipeline page: `GET /runners/monitor` now carries each assignment's own project/task/stage identity, the widget renders it even when the viewer looks at another pipeline, and "Open task" jumps to the job in its pipeline (task 350ca162).
- Bottom-bar queue number counts only tasks waiting to be picked up (never running, blocked, paused, failed, cancelled, or waiting-human tasks), and the queue popup lists exactly that same set in dispatch order (task 6d3c9317).
- Survey answers survive later Runner stages: Runner task-file shipments merge into the backend survey (new rounds land, saved answers are kept) instead of overwriting them with stale worktree copies; the question-me prompt also names the exact backend-resolved file for alias/extension-less configs (task fbcaef1d).
